result.markdown: --- title: "[MaxComboResult]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} The outcome of a MaxCombo weighted log-rank test. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_tests.py#L137-L193){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python MaxComboResult(statistic, p_value, z_statistics, correlation, method) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The MaxCombo test is designed to detect survival differences under non-proportional hazards by combining multiple Fleming-Harrington weight functions. The test statistic is the maximum absolute Z across the weight set, and the p-value accounts for the correlation between the Z-statistics. ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [statistic]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The MaxCombo test statistic: the maximum absolute Z-statistic across the weight functions. [p_value]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : P-value from the multivariate normal distribution. The probability of observing a max |Z| this large or larger under the null hypothesis. [z_statistics]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[tuple[float, float], float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary mapping each (rho, gamma) weight tuple to its Z-statistic. [correlation]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Array]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Correlation matrix between the Z-statistics under H0, as a NumPy array. [method]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Human-readable description of the test. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Run a MaxCombo test on the `lung` dataset, comparing survival by sex. The result holds the Z-statistics for each weight function and the combined p-value: ::: {#8edd574b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") mc = gw.maxcombo_test("Surv(time, status) ~ sex", data=lung) mc ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` MaxComboResult(statistic=3.5657, p_value=0.0009956, weights=[(0, 0), (1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1)]) ``` ::: ::: Inspect the per-weight Z-statistics: ::: {#0318d14f .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} mc.z_statistics ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {(0, 0): 3.21352484896035, (1, 0): 3.565690872910549, (0, 1): 1.8601032675878904, (1, 1): 2.7685344459841996} ``` ::: :::
